title: Purchase Order
context: Material Management › Procure-to-Pay (PO Flow) › Purchase Order

cards.title: Where the Purchase Order sits in the procurement workflow
cards.body:
The Purchase Order represents step eight in the ten-step procurement sequence within Material Management.
It immediately follows the Comparative Statement where vendor quotes are analyzed and ranked.
Upon creation, the purchase order becomes the official commercial commitment issued to the approved supplier.
The next physical step in the workflow is Gate Entry when ordered goods arrive at the factory gate.
Purchase officers draft the order, while authorized purchase managers grant final commercial approval.
The order takes approved rates and delivery schedules from preceding quotations and departmental indents.
Authorized purchase orders serve as the mandatory reference for incoming consignments at the factory gate.
Without an authorized order, security personnel cannot log incoming consignments into the facility.
Delivery schedules, freight conditions, and payment terms recorded here govern downstream receipt and billing.
The order ensures all organizational procurement adheres strictly to approved budgets and operational authorizations.
Physical verification against this document ensures company commitments match agreed commercial terms.
Once released, the purchase order provides legal documentation protecting both buyer and supplier interests.
Commercial terms established on this document cannot be altered without formal management authorization.
Any modification creates a new revision record maintaining an auditable track of revisions.
These governance controls prevent unauthorized price escalations and enforce corporate procurement discipline.

cards.title: Mandatory commercial header fields and reference selections
cards.body:
The system enforces strict completeness rules before a purchase order can be saved in the system.
The user must select a valid document type, purchase category, and reference document type from master options.
Selecting a verified vendor and associated location is mandatory for all procurement transactions.
The validity date must be specified and cannot precede the current document date under any circumstances.
If the validity date is earlier than the document date, the system immediately halts the save operation.
A valid operational department and purchase organization must be linked to establish internal accountability.
If the vendor contact person is missing, the system prompts the user with an explicit confirmation warning.
When referencing an existing contract, the document date must fall strictly within the active contract period.
Duplicate document numbers are prohibited by automated yearly numbering validation enforced on save.
Every purchase order must link to at least one valid line item with positive quantity and agreed unit price.
Missing mandatory headers halt saving and highlight the exact commercial information requiring user entry.
These checks prevent incomplete or unauthorized purchase orders from being dispatched to external vendors.

cards.title: Quantity tolerance thresholds and item rate integrity checks
cards.body:
Every line item must satisfy defined commercial tolerances, item specifications, and rate validation checks.
Ordered quantities cannot exceed the remaining open balance of the referenced indent or quotation.
Negative tolerance cannot equal or exceed one hundred percent of the line quantity on any row.
Positive tolerance governs the maximum acceptable over-delivery during subsequent warehouse receipt.
The unit rate cannot be left empty or set to zero for standard commercial purchase lines.
When standard rate validation is enabled, the entered rate cannot exceed the master standard rate.
Items classified as capital goods cannot be mixed with standard operational consumables on the same order.
Duplicate items sharing identical technical specifications and makes are prevented on the same document.
Conversion factors between purchasing and stocking units must be non-zero positive numbers.
These checks prevent over-ordering and enforce adherence to negotiated corporate purchasing agreements.
Tolerance parameters protect the business against unexpected price escalations and unauthorized vendor over-shipments.
Every line item must also link to an active tax classification heading before commercial authorization.
These tolerance rules ensure delivery quantities remain aligned with contractual vendor agreements.
Unauthorized excess shipments are rejected at warehouse intake, preventing unbudgeted inventory holding.
Accurate unit rates ensure that inventory valuation models accurately reflect negotiated terms.

cards.title: Authorization workflow stages and record locking mechanisms
cards.body:
Purchase orders move through three distinct operational states: Initial, Release, and Authorized.
Newly created orders reside in Initial status where field modifications remain unlocked for editing.
Submitting for approval advances the status to Release, locking general editing for regular purchasing clerks.
Under multi-tier authorization groups, each designated manager must log approval sequentially by tier.
The system halts approval if an intermediate user attempts to bypass preceding approval levels.
The document status cannot be manually marked Authorized under multi-tier workflows.
Only the final designated approval level transitions the order into Authorized status.
Once authorized, the purchase order is completely locked against direct edits, line modifications, or deletion.
If amendments are required, an authorized amendment document must be raised through formal revision channels.
Cancelled or completed purchase orders cannot be re-authorized or modified by any user in the organization.
This state progression ensures that purchasing commitments undergo rigorous executive review before vendor issuance.
Locked records preserve an immutable audit trail for internal accounting and external financial compliance.
Automated notifications inform designated approvers when pending documents require their authorization.
Approvers can review budget consumption and vendor performance history before approving.
This strict hierarchy guarantees that organizational expenditures adhere strictly to delegated financial limits.

cards.title: Logistics routing parameters and freight expense controls
cards.body:
Logistics details establish freight liabilities, carrier responsibilities, and physical delivery destinations.
Users specify transportation mode, freight payment responsibility, and verified delivery locations.
The system prevents the origin location and destination location from being identical on any route.
Freight expenses cannot be defined concurrently as both a fixed amount and an independent freight order.
Transportation routes cannot be assigned to orders categorized under capital procurement.
When discrete raw materials are selected, standard transportation routing is disallowed by system checks.
Consignee delivery locations must be valid and linked to active company operational divisions.
Freight charges defined on the order automatically default into subsequent receipt documents for reconciliation.
These logistics rules ensure accurate cost allocation and clear carrier responsibilities across transport legs.
Inaccurate route definitions prevent transaction saving until location and expense conflicts are resolved.
Correct logistics mapping ensures arriving consignments are directed smoothly to the correct factory unloading bay.
Transportation terms established here govern how freight invoices are later passed in accounts payable.
Designating clear shipping routes reduces freight transit times and minimizes logistics expenses.
Carriers must confirm route compliance and delivery checkpoints upon consignment arrival.
These logistics details ensure transport liabilities and demurrage costs are assigned correctly.

cards.title: Goods and services tax determination and vendor advance rules
cards.body:
Tax structures are evaluated automatically based on vendor registration and company delivery site.
Interstate purchases require integrated tax, while intrastate purchases apply central and state taxes.
Applying state tax to an interstate purchase triggers an immediate validation refusal on save.
Each line item must possess an active harmonized system code linked to the material item master.
When vendor advances exist, users can allocate open advance balances against the purchase order.
The adjusted advance amount cannot exceed the open balance of the referenced advance payment.
Total advance adjustments cannot exceed the net payable commercial value of the purchase order.
Unadjusted advances generate confirmation warnings prior to completing the save operation.
Tax concessions require valid statutory exemption forms to be linked to the tax schedule.
Accurate tax and advance reconciliation prevents invoice disputes during financial settlement in accounts payable.
These fiscal controls ensure full compliance with national revenue authorities and statutory tax reporting.
Correct tax scheduling guarantees that input tax credits are claimed accurately by the finance team.
Clear advance allocation prevents double disbursement and reduces outstanding supplier liability balances.
Reconciled tax entries ensure the company claims eligible statutory credits without dispute.
These financial controls protect company cash flow and maintain transparent vendor accounts.

cards.title: System deletion prohibitions and dependency safeguards
cards.body:
The system enforces referential integrity to protect active commercial commitments and audit lineage.
A purchase order cannot be deleted if subsequent amendment entries have been recorded against it.
Orders created against letters of intent cannot be deleted while the letter remains active.
If a vendor advance payment request has been prepared against the order, deletion is blocked.
The presence of an active bank guarantee tied to the order also prevents document deletion.
Authorized orders cannot be removed from the system under any operational circumstances.
Attempting to delete a referenced order generates an explicit system refusal message detailing dependencies.
These restrictions prevent accidental removal of legally binding corporate agreements and procurement history.
Users must formally cancel open line balances rather than attempting to delete historical records.
Audit trails preserve all authorized order history for financial compliance, internal audit, and supplier tracking.
Deleting draft records is restricted to authorized purchasing personnel before commercial release.
This referential protection guarantees that upstream indents and downstream receipts remain perfectly synchronized.
System safeguards guarantee that legal commitments cannot be wiped out by operational personnel.
Historical procurement data remains accessible for vendor performance evaluations and internal reviews.
This referential protection ensures complete operational transparency across the procurement lifecycle.
